objective: Port netty-testsuite-common 4.2.19.Final (io.netty.util.test: the JUnit 5 leak presence extension and DisabledForSlowLeakDetection) to the test-support library Netty.NET.Testsuite.Common for xUnit v3, and run the tests of every module whose Java tests depend on it with the extension.

review.scope: The annotation is a static class: an xUnit attribute cannot carry the @DisabledIf condition, so a test (or every test of a class, the annotation's TYPE target) is marked [Fact(Skip = DisabledForSlowLeakDetection.Reason, SkipType = typeof(DisabledForSlowLeakDetection), SkipWhen = nameof(DisabledForSlowLeakDetection.SlowLeakDetection))]; Reason is the text JUnit reports for a @DisabledIf without disabledReason. Helper keeps its detector of the Helper type, and slowLeakDetection() is DETECTOR.IsRecordEnabled(). The four Java users (AdaptiveByteBufAllocatorGrowthTest, AdaptiveByteBufAllocatorTest, codec-compression AbstractIntegrationTest and codec-http HttpContentDecompressorTest) carry the skip condition; with the presence detector it is false and they run.

The JUnit callbacks are static members that the CLR-only LeakPresenceTestFramework (an xUnit v3 test framework registered with [assembly: TestFramework], LeakPresenceExtension.props) runs around each test class: BeforeAll before the default class runner (class fixtures, instances, tests, fixture disposal) and AfterAll after it, whose failure is a test collection cleanup failure that names the class scope (the run fails with exit code 1; the message shows with the console logger at normal verbosity). The InheritableThreadLocal is an AsyncLocal that the ExecutionContext carries into the tests, their Tasks, thread-pool work and started threads, so beforeEach and afterEach have no counterpart. The static SCOPE of the generic WithTransferableScope<T> is in a non-generic WithTransferableScope (CLR generic statics exist per constructed type). The custom detector property is the environment variable io.netty.customResourceLeakDetector, set to the assembly-qualified name of the generic definition before any detector exists (framework constructor). Boolean.getBoolean accepts only "true". xUnit has no @Nested lifecycle: a nested class is a test class with its own scope; the owner checks stay. With the disabled property the framework is xUnit's own, as the leak profile runs without autodetection. With trackCreationStack the creation stacks (suppressed exceptions) become inner exceptions of the reported failure. Measured 2026-11-27: a constructor-allocated tracker and an unreleased default-allocator buffer each fail the run with "Possible memory leak detected for resource scope '<class>'".

caseMappings.adaptation: EngineTestKit (org.junit.platform.testkit) has no xUnit v3 counterpart, so the test drives the lifecycle JUnit runs for the selected class through the extension members, in a flow without a scope as LeakPresenceTestFramework starts a class, and asserts what the source checks through the events: no failure, the tests run in the class scope, and only the owner closes it (an allocation in the closed scope throws AllocationProhibitedException). The @Nested InnerTest runs inside the outer lifecycle: BeforeAll reuses the outer scope, and AfterAll of the nested class leaves it open.

The property is the environment variable, set to "true" and restored; the skipped container is EvaluateExecutionCondition returning false with the source reason (and true with "Leak presence detection enabled" afterwards). @ExtendWith has no counterpart: LeakPresenceTestFramework applies the extension only while the condition is true.
